bio: Miro is a Quebec singer, rapper and songwriter whose music blends pop, R&B and hip-hop. His francophone catalogue has earned recognition within Quebec's music industry, including ADISQ attention, while maintaining a contemporary crossover sound. Northern Dial carries Miro as part of its Quebec pop and R&B catalogue.

Northern British Columbia duo Mob Bounce is an Indigenous Canadian hip-hop group formed by Gitxsan artist The Northwest Kid and Cree-Métis artist EarthChild, blending electronic beats with culture, healing and social justice.
Montréal band Mobile is a Canadian alternative-rock group whose debut album Tomorrow Starts Today earned major radio play and the Juno Award for New Group of the Year.

Moist emerged from Vancouver in the early 1990s and quickly became one of the bands that defined Canada's alternative-rock boom. Fronted by David Usher, with Mark Makoway, Jeff Pearce, Kevin Young and Paul Wilcox in the group's best-known early lineup, Moist broke nationally with the 1994 album Silver. Songs such as "Push," the title track and "Believe Me" turned the band into a MuchMusic and rock-radio fixture, while its dramatic, atmospheric sound helped distinguish Vancouver's contribution to a decade often dominated in the Canadian imagination by Toronto and Kingston rock scenes.

The band's second album, Creature, expanded that reach with a darker, more polished sound and earned an Album of the Year nomination at the 1998 JUNO Awards. Moist also received JUNO recognition across the decade, including a Best New Group nomination in 1995, Group of the Year recognition and a Rock Album nomination for 1999's Mercedes Five and Dime. By then, Usher's increasingly visible solo career was running alongside the band, and Moist eventually went inactive in the early 2000s.

The group reunited in the 2010s and released Glory Under Dangerous Skies in 2014, followed by End of the Ocean in 2022. Those later records did not attempt to recreate the 1990s moment so much as extend a catalogue that already occupies an important place in Canadian alternative-rock history. Moist belongs to the generation that turned domestic radio, MuchMusic exposure and national touring into a sustainable Canadian rock ecosystem, and its reunion-era work has kept that history active rather than purely nostalgic.

Born Daniel Denton and raised in British Columbia, Moka Only began recording well before Vancouver hip-hop had much national infrastructure. He became part of the city's underground network in the 1990s, recording solo material, working in groups including the early Swollen Members lineup and developing a self-contained approach in which rapping, singing and beatmaking were all parts of the same practice. His 1995 debut Upcoast Relix began a catalogue that would grow at an extraordinary pace, with independent tapes, albums, collaborations and instrumental projects arriving far more frequently than the conventional label cycle allowed.

Moka's best-known mainstream chapter came through Swollen Members. He rejoined the group during its early-2000s commercial breakthrough and appeared on releases including Monsters in the Closet and Heavy, a period that brought major Canadian exposure and multiple Juno wins around the group. But the larger story of his career is the solo work around and after that success. Albums such as The Desired Effect, Vermilion and the long-running Airport series moved between jazzy sample-based production, synthesizers, singing, understated rhyme writing and deliberately low-key experimentation. By 2011, Exclaim! was already describing a discography of more than 60 albums, collaborative projects and beat tapes.

That volume is not simply a novelty. Moka Only's catalogue represents a durable model of independent Canadian hip-hop built around self-production, home recording and constant stylistic movement rather than a handful of flagship releases. His collaborations have connected him with artists including J Dilla, MF DOOM, Kool Keith and Del the Funky Homosapien, while later records such as Summer 2002 and In and of Itself have continued the same self-directed approach decades into his career. His significance to Canadian rap comes from both sides of that history: participation in one of Vancouver's biggest crossover groups and an unusually deep underground catalogue that kept expanding long after the major-label spotlight moved elsewhere.

MOMONEYMATTEO is a Canadian independent hip-hop artist from the north end of Halifax. His catalogue connects Halifax's contemporary rap scene with wider underground hip-hop networks, including his appearance alongside Chuuwee and Eddie Kaine on DK's 2023 track 'Gold Tooth' from Atlantic Rap Vol. 1. The collaboration places him in a cross-border East Coast context while his own artist profile identifies Halifax as his home base and origin.

Mister Monark is a Fredericton, New Brunswick hip-hop artist associated with Atlantic Canada's long-running underground rap scene. His work includes collaborations with artists such as Phakt and Sean One, and he has appeared on projects and compilations documenting Canadian rap from Fredericton and Saint John. Northern Dial carries Monark as part of its East Coast Canadian hip-hop catalogue.

Money Musik, born Mohkom Singh Bhangal, is a Brampton, Ontario producer whose early work with Toronto artists including Pressa, WhyG, Casper TNG and LB Spiffy grew into an international production career. He became a key collaborator of NAV and produced the full AP Dhillon and Gurinder Gill album Not by Chance. Northern Dial carries one of the AP Dhillon, Gurinder Gill and Money Musik recordings from that era.

Scarborough collective Monolith is a Canadian hip-hop crew formed in the 1990s from members of Lyrical Coalition and The Horde, with a deep roster of rappers, DJs and producers tied to Toronto's underground scene.

Monolith: IRS is a catalogue credit for the IRS branch of Toronto's Monolith hip-hop collective. IRS members Korry Deez, Black Cat and T.R.A.C.K.S. came out of Monolith before establishing the Canadian trio behind Welcome to Planet IRS, and later reunited with fellow Monolith MCs on Wio-K's Ten.
Winnipeg group Mood Ruff was a pioneering Canadian hip-hop act known for socially conscious lyricism, grassroots touring and an important role in Manitoba's independent rap scene.

Morbid Concepts is a Canadian hip-hop act from the early-2000s underground scene, documented through the 2003 release The Arrival and collaborations with Divo. The project's catalogue includes 'Got it Locked Down' with Divo and 'Master of Ceremonies' with Classified and Sharky, and Morbid Concepts also appears on Divo's 'Reservoir Dawgs' and 'Move (Remix)'.
Toronto rapper, DJ and producer More Or Les is a Canadian underground hip-hop artist and Backburner member known for witty lyricism, turntablism and a long independent catalogue.

Toronto-born Wendy 'Motion' Brathwaite is a Canadian emcee, spoken-word poet, playwright, screenwriter and activist whose work has helped connect hip-hop, literature and theatre for more than three decades. A co-founder of CIUT's long-running Masterplan Show and a member of Nu Black Nation, she made Canadian hip-hop history with early releases including Use What U Got and later expanded into award-winning film and television writing.
Canadian rapper Mr. Roam is a veteran of Toronto hip-hop whose work helped connect Ghetto Concept, Da Grassroots and the city's late-1990s independent rap movement.

Ms. Bella is a Canadian francophone urban-pop singer-songwriter based in Montréal. Previously recording as Angee Wings, she relaunched her career as Ms. Bella and has worked across acoustic pop, dancehall and afropop with Québec producers including Kleancut, Poirier and Sonny Black. Northern Dial carries her single 'Désert', which is also documented in SiriusXM Influence Franco airplay listings.
Saskatoon-born, Toronto-based producer and rapper Muneshine is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose career spans solo work, production, DJing and collaborations across Canada's independent rap scene.

Formed in Montréal in 1996 by J.Kyll, Imposs and Dramatik, Muzion became one of the foundational groups of Québec hip-hop by making the city's Haitian diaspora central to the music rather than peripheral to it. The trio moved naturally among French, English and Haitian Creole, bringing the language and experience of neighbourhoods including Saint-Michel into a Québec rap landscape that was still defining itself. Their 1999 debut Mentalité moune morne… (Ils n'ont pas compris) paired dense, socially engaged writing with a distinctly Montréal perspective and won the Félix for Hip-Hop Album of the Year, establishing Muzion as both a critical force and a cultural point of identification for Black and immigrant audiences in Québec.

Their second album, J'rêvolutionne, followed in 2002 and also earned a Félix for Hip-Hop Album of the Year. The group's most enduring anthem, "La vi ti nèg," fused hip-hop with kompa and celebrated Haitian life in Montréal with a combination of resilience, neighbourhood pride and joy. The song won a Canadian Urban Music Award in 2004, and its influence continued long after Muzion's initial recording run: in 2025, SOCAN gave "La vi ti nèg" its Cultural Impact Award, the first time the honour had gone to a hip-hop song in the gala's history. Artists from later generations of Québec rap have repeatedly identified Muzion as proof that their own communities, accents and cultural references could belong in the province's mainstream music conversation.

That legacy received another national acknowledgement in January 2026, when Canada Post honoured Muzion alongside Maestro Fresh Wes and Michie Mee in a Black History Month stamp series celebrating Canadian hip-hop trailblazers. For Northern Dial, Muzion matters because they connect several histories at once: the rise of francophone rap, Montréal's Haitian cultural presence, women in Québec hip-hop through J.Kyll's visibility, and a broader Canadian story in which local identity became a source of musical authority rather than something artists had to dilute to be heard.
Montréal-born singer-songwriter Myles Lloyd is a Canadian R&B artist whose melodic, emotionally candid music explores relationships, vulnerability and modern soul production.

Ches Christian, better known as N.I.F.T.Y., is a Toronto faith-based hip-hop artist, storyteller and educator with a recording career stretching back to the 2000s. Alongside national touring and independent releases including This Iz Bizness, he became Canada's first rap performance professor at Centennial College and has remained active in music education and community work.
Vancouver collective NADUH is a Canadian femme-led R&B and hip-hop group that writes, engineers and produces its own music around themes of empowerment, queerness and collective creativity.

Montreal-based Nana Quinn is a multidisciplinary Quebec artist, writer and musician whose work moves between poetry, performance, visual art and experimental folk-pop. A Radio-Canada poetry prize recipient and CALQ-supported artist, Quinn has released books alongside musical projects including tout me quitte / tout vient à moi.

Montréal-based Iraqi-Canadian rapper, writer, professor and multidisciplinary artist Narcy, born Yassin Alsalman, is a pioneering voice in Arab hip-hop whose work spans music, film, education and cultural production.
Waterloo, Ontario singer-songwriter Nate Haller is a Canadian country artist known for energetic live shows, contemporary country production and a run of nationally charting singles.

Montréal rapper Nate Husser, born Nathaniel Huskinson, first emerged with The Posterz before developing a solo catalogue that moves between melodic rap, alternative hip-hop and bilingual collaborations.

Nathan Allen is a contemporary jazz saxophonist from Brampton, Ontario whose sound blends smooth jazz, R&B and hip-hop influences. He studied at York University in Toronto and built a large online audience through saxophone performances and covers, while continuing to perform regularly across the Greater Toronto Area. Northern Dial carries Nathan Allen as part of its contemporary Canadian jazz and instrumental catalogue.

Toronto-born Navraj Singh Goraya, known as NAV, came up in Rexdale as both a producer and recording artist. His earliest industry attention came behind the boards before his own hazy, Auto-Tuned records began circulating online, eventually bringing him into The Weeknd's XO ecosystem. The 2017 self-titled NAV project and Metro Boomin collaboration Perfect Timing established his minimalist melodic-trap vocabulary, built around subdued delivery, spacious production and an intentionally detached persona.

RECKLESS broadened his major-label catalogue, but 2019's Bad Habits marked the commercial leap: the album debuted at No. 1 on both the Billboard Canadian Albums chart and the U.S. Billboard 200. NAV subsequently sustained that audience with projects including Good Intentions, Demons Protected by Angels and OMW2 Rexdale, while high-profile collaborations with artists such as Travis Scott, Gunna and Lil Uzi Vert kept his production and vocals circulating through the wider American rap ecosystem. His appearance on Internet Money's "Lemonade" also reached the Billboard Hot 100 Top 10.

NAV occupies a distinct place in Canadian hip-hop history. He is one of the first Punjabi-Canadian rappers to become a consistent commercial presence at the highest level of North American rap, and his career reflects Toronto's transformation from a city seeking U.S. validation into a city capable of feeding artists directly into global streaming culture. His understated vocal style has been divisive, but the longevity and chart scale of his catalogue make his significance difficult to reduce to taste alone.

Nawfal is a Montreal rapper whose work sits in contemporary francophone hip-hop, often drawing on Maghrebi identity and local Quebec culture. His releases include SECTEUR NORD, L.X.I.V and the 2025 project blues beldi with producer Kheir; their track archive 2001 is the Northern Dial library entry.

Montreal singer-songwriter Naïma Frank is a rising voice in Quebec's francophone R&B scene, blending alternative R&B, pop, electro, hip-hop and jazz influences with writing shaped by her Haitian heritage. Her debut album 18 ans et + arrived in 2026 after the acclaimed EP Petite fille devient grande.
Toronto group Nefarius was a Canadian underground hip-hop act from the 1990s whose members included producer Don D, later of Tone Mason, and MCs Collizhun and Kwesro.
Halifax-formed Canadian alt-pop duo Neon Dreams, led by Frank Kadillac and Adrian Morris, makes expansive pop shaped by electronic production and a wide range of rock, folk and rhythmic influences.
Neverending White Lights is the Canadian collaborative project of Windsor-born multi-instrumentalist and producer Daniel Victor, pairing cinematic alternative rock with rotating guest vocalists.
Toronto singer-songwriter NIA NADURATA is a Canadian indie-pop artist whose guitar-led writing and contemporary R&B touches have built a growing audience since her 2023 solo debut.
Gatineau-born, Montréal-based producer Nicholas Craven is known for soulful, gritty sample-chop production and an extensive catalogue with leading voices in contemporary underground hip-hop.

Nick Day is a singer and guitarist from Sandy Lake First Nation in Ontario who performed with the Indigenous rock group Bear Paws. The group recorded the rare 1988 album Kitche-Ogamah for Sunshine Records, blending original material with rock and country influences. Northern Dial carries Nick Day as part of its archival Indigenous Canadian music catalogue.
Salt Spring Island singer-songwriter Nicky MacKenzie is a Canadian R&B and soul artist whose jazzy vocals and pop songwriting developed through British Columbia's emerging-artist scene.
Montréal singer-songwriter Nicola Ciccone is an Italian-Canadian francophone artist whose multilingual pop catalogue has produced dozens of Québec radio hits across more than two decades.
Toronto-born singer and television host Nicole Holness is a Canadian R&B artist known for her work in the group X-Quisite and her later broadcasting career.
Montréal singer Nikki Yanofsky is a Canadian jazz-pop vocalist who emerged as a teenage prodigy and later performed the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics broadcast anthem I Believe.

Galyn Esmé, better known as NiLLa, is a Canadian hip-hop emcee, producer, educator and photographer based in Toronto. Active for more than 15 years, she built a reputation for conscious lyricism and self-produced music, won Rap/Hip-Hop Recording of the Year at the Hamilton Music Awards for From the Ground UP and has performed across Canada and Europe.
Toronto Japanese-Canadian rapper Nish Raawks, born Derek Nishikawa, is a member of the Monolith collective whose work helped shape the city's independent hip-hop scene.

Noam is a Toronto singer, songwriter and producer whose independent work blends contemporary songwriting with self-produced arrangements. His Toronto-based catalogue spans original recordings and production work released through his own artist channels. Northern Dial carries Noam as part of its Toronto independent music catalogue.
Bow Island, Alberta singer-songwriter Noeline Hofmann is a Canadian country and western artist whose traditional songwriting gained international attention through the song Purple Gas.

NojokeJigsaw is a Toronto rapper and songwriter from Lawrence Heights, the community widely known as Jungle. Emerging in 2017, he developed an independent catalogue through Restless Records that includes It's Complicated and the Late Nights Early Mornings series, with music shaped by his experiences growing up in Toronto's northwest end.
Gananoque, Ontario singer-songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist Nolan Hubbard is a Canadian artist whose music blends soul, pop, rock and live-looping performance.

Nonso Amadi is a Nigerian-born, Toronto-based Afro-R&B singer, songwriter and producer whose music blends contemporary R&B, soul, Afrobeats and alté influences. After moving to Canada, he developed a cross-continental career that has included a JUNO nomination and releases through Universal Music Canada. DROWN from his 2025 EP TO CRY A FLOOD is his Northern Dial library credit.

NorthSideBaby, born Dawson Pastion-Bear in High Level, Alberta, is an Indigenous Canadian rapper and producer from Dene Tha’ First Nation. After beginning as a teenage beatmaker, he moved into recording his own vocals and built a touring career that has taken him through communities and cities across Canada.
